name: Vitality Bowls
blocked: Chain franchise, address 8935 Towne Centre Dr Ste 107 confirmed via web search snippets matching exactly. Own site's ordering is an Incentivio JS SPA (order.incentivio.com/c/vitalitybowls/locations/vitalitybowlssandiegoca) that returns only an empty app shell to a plain fetch - no server-rendered menu or reachable API. Own site's static /menu/ page lists the national create-your-own-bowl template with calories but explicitly no prices (franchise pricing varies by location, as is typical for this chain). DoorDash storefront for this exact location (vitality-bowls-san-diego-75253) exists and was found via search, but every direct fetch attempt (3 tries, different UA/referer) hit a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' JS challenge that curl cannot solve. Uber Eats storefront URL found via search 404s on direct fetch (same as other Uber Eats stores in this batch that require a real browser session). A web-search AI summary quoted possible prices (Vitality Bowl $13.49, Nutty Bowl $13.99, Superfood Bowl $17.99) but these were not independently confirmed against a fetched structured payload, so not filed per the no-constructed-prices rule. Worth a retry with a real browser/session for DoorDash or Uber Eats.

name: Kearny Mesa Brothers Mexican Restaurant
notes: Own domain (brothersmexicanfood3ca.com), site displays as 'Brother's Mexican Food 3' at 8042 Clairemont Mesa Blvd - matches work-list address exactly (also confirmed via embedded lat/long marker and hidden lid form fields). Homepage only shows a 3-item 'Popular Items' teaser; the full priced menu is on a separate route (/brothers-mexican-food-3/menu/) reached by trying likely paths since it wasn't linked directly in the crawled homepage HTML. This is the restaurant's own first-party order-ahead system (white-label platform branded 'fromtherestaurant.com'/'arctic_app' embedded in the page, not a third-party delivery marketplace), so no delivery-fee-markup motive applies. 268 priced items across 25 categories (breakfast plates/burritos, tostadas, soups, seafood, burritos, chimichangas, carne asada fries/chips, surf and turf, tortas, taco salads, super quesadillas, combination plates, tacos, salads, super tostadas, hamburgers, brothers specials, party packs, kids, sides, extras, drinks, plus a weekly/Fri-Sat fish special). Cents are unusually specific and scattered (e.g. $17.60, $16.52, $5.20) rather than round - ran a markup-divisor sweep (1.00-1.40) and a flat-subtraction sweep across all 268 prices and found no single factor that converts them to a round base (best divisor only explained ~23% of prices, i.e. noise-level) - concluded this is just the restaurant's own idiosyncratic cost-based pricing, not evidence of fee-inflation, and filed as-is.
